dedupe_keys.name: mitre att ck for ics knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against industrial control systems

description: MITRE ATT&CK for ICS is a curated knowledge base of the tactics and techniques that adversaries use against industrial control systems, built from public reporting of real incidents. It is produced and maintained by The MITRE Corporation with contributions from the security community, as one of the three ATT&CK matrices alongside Enterprise and Mobile. Coverage: global, drawing on incidents in power, water, oil and gas, manufacturing and other sectors. The ICS matrix arranges techniques under twelve tactics, from initial access and execution to inhibit response function, impair process control and impact, and links them to mitigations, targeted assets such as controllers, safety systems and HMIs, detection strategies and data components, threat groups, malware and named campaigns. Format and access: web pages, the ATT&CK Navigator for annotating matrices, a Workbench application, Python utilities, Excel files and machine-readable STIX 2.1 bundles in MITRE's GitHub repositories; versioned releases; free. Licence: MITRE's royalty-free licence for research, development and commercial use, provided the copyright notice and licence are reproduced. Caveats: coverage reflects publicly reported incidents, so techniques used in unreported attacks are missing, and entries describe behaviours, not vulnerability or asset data. Simulation uses: structuring cyber attack scenarios for cascading failure and resilience models of control systems, and mapping testbed attacks to known techniques. Related records: the ITI ICS packet captures (data-iti-ics-security-tools-pcaps) and the architectural weaknesses dataset (data-ics-advisories-architectural-security-weaknesses) are complementary sources for control system security.
